rationale: The workflow is a reusable workflow_call with three jobs. The two dependency-heavy jobs (check-and-lint, check-tests) already use jdx/mise-action with cache: true, which caches installed tools and their downloads (cargo-deny, osv-scanner, uv) across runs. The script_tests job uses system Python with unittest and installs no dependencies. The closest pattern, P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency download cache), is not applied because its contraindication "An equivalent cache already exists" is satisfied by the existing mise cache, and adding actions/cache would be redundant and risks caching unchecked build outputs. No matrix exists, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply. As a workflow_call with no direct push/pull_request triggers, trigger-based patterns (cancel-stale, change-filter, skip-workflow) do not apply to this file. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT was considered, but the history shows short, consistently successful runs (~5 min); a timeout is a guardrail rather than a normal-case optimization, and no runaway-job evidence justifies imposing one. No supported, non-redundant optimization preserves coverage while improving this workflow, so the workflow is left unchanged.
